description: 2 tactical challenges for White against the Blackburne Shilling Gambit. Meet 3...Nd4 with calm development and refuse the poisoned pawn.

drills.briefExplanation: 3.Bc4 Nd4 4.O-O! Nxf3+ 5.Qxf3 — castle first, take back with the queen, ignore the bait.
drills.description: White to play. Black may try the tricky 3...Nd4 — develop 3.Bc4 and answer with 4.O-O!.
drills.explanation: The refutation of the Shilling is beautifully simple: don't take on e5. After 3...Nd4 White plays 4.O-O!, castling straight through the provocation. If 4...Nxf3+ 5.Qxf3 White is simply better — king safe, queen developed, no tricks remaining. The gambit only works if White gets greedy; calm development kills it.
drills.name: Refusing the Pawn

drills.briefExplanation: 4.c3 Nxf3+ 5.Qxf3 Qf6 6.d4! — strike in the center before Black consolidates.
drills.description: White to play. You've played 4.c3 against 3...Nd4 — now meet 4...Nxf3+ correctly.
drills.explanation: After 4.c3 Nxf3+ 5.Qxf3 Qf6 Black's queen looks active, but White has the antidote: 6.d4! strikes in the center, opening lines while Black is still undeveloped. The queen on f6 will have to move again, White gains time, and the 'active' queen becomes a target. Central counterplay beats flank provocation.
drills.name: The d4 Break
